author: claude-prob1000-D-0908
key_identity: d_gamma = 2Q/xi with Q = 2/gamma + gamma/2; d_{sqrt(8/3)} = 4 is known only through the Brownian map bijections.
method: Ask what kind of object d_gamma is. The known relations are d_gamma = 2 Q / xi with Q = 2/gamma + gamma/2, so a formula for d_gamma is the same as a formula for the LFPP exponent xi in terms of gamma. The exponent xi is defined by a subadditive limit for the LFPP distance, so it is a Lyapunov-type exponent for a multiplicative cascade of Gaussian weights.
obstruction: The wall is that no exactly solvable structure is known for the LQG metric away from gamma = sqrt(8/3). Every exponent that has been computed in LQG (measure exponents, the KPZ relation, ball boundary dimensions) is a consequence of the multiplicative structure of the MEASURE, which is exactly solvable; the metric is a first-passage time and is not a function of the measure. This is the same wall that prevents computing the time constant in ordinary first-passage percolation, and there is no reason to think the LQG case is easier except that its environment is exactly scale invariant.
result: The honest structural statement is that d_gamma is a first-passage percolation time constant for a log-correlated environment, and the only quantity of that type with a known closed form in two dimensions is the sqrt(8/3) case, which is known NOT from the metric side at all but from the Brownian-map bijections. That is a strong warning against expecting a closed form: the value 4 is a combinatorial output of the Schaeffer bijection, and no bijection is available for other gamma. Two soft constraints I can record: (i) d_gamma is strictly increasing in gamma (Ding-Gwynne), continuous, with d_0+ = 2 and d_{2-} = 4 * something at criticality; (ii) the Watabiki prediction is false at small gamma (Ding-Goswami), so any conjectural formula must fail to match Watabiki near gamma = 0, which rules out the whole family of formulas obtained by analytic continuation of the Watabiki ansatz.
